To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

students who are taught to solve multistep equations by using the virtual manipulative, the algebraic method, and the algebraic method with the virtual manipulative outperformed students in the traditional instruction group on a posttest of multistep equations.

(1) students with LDs who receive explicit instruction in algebraic problem solving and who are provided with a variety of opportunities to practice solving problems in the context of real-world situations, can be successful in solving algebraic equations and inequalities; (2) the use of virtual manipulatives to represent and solve algebraic equations and algebraic inequalities can help secondary students with LDs to develop a deeper understanding of the concepts and procedures of algebra and to develop a greater appreciation for the utility of algebra
The results showed that the students who were exposed to the treatment group had a significantly higher mean score on the pretest and post-test compared to the control group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the teaching of algebraic concepts to students with disabilities, particularly students who are at risk for mathematics failure.
the use of the sequence and strategic instruction (SSI) model for teaching multistep equations.
the use of virtual manipulatives in teaching algebraic concepts to secondary students with learning disabilities.

the students in the experimental group performed better than the students in the control group in solving multistep equations.
the use of virtual manipulatives is a useful and effective strategy to teach multistep equations to secondary students with learning disabilities.
virtual manipulatives are a valuable tool to use in teaching students with learning disabilities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an approach to teaching algebraic concepts that is effective for students with disabilities, and that the approach is also effective with students without disabilities.
we have developed and evaluated a new instructional model for teaching algebraic problem solving to students with disabilities, which we call the Algebraic Problem Solving Model (APS model).
we found a significant effect for the use of virtual manipulatives on students with learning disabilities in mathematics.

the use of virtual manipulatives in teaching multistep equations to secondary students with learning disabilities is a promising practice.
